CHOICE.COM.note: Optional prompt text combines with choice-list, display, sensitivity, timeout, redirected-input, validation, and index-errorlevel behavior

COMP.COM.note: Up to two filespecs plus the interactive missing-operand and repeat workflows

DEBUG.COM.note: Filename startup processing followed by a source-dispatched interactive command language

EMM386.EXE.note: The installed dual-purpose image reports live DOS 6 EMS statistics and accepts ON, OFF, AUTO, W=ON, and W=OFF runtime control keywords with reference-style invalid-parameter diagnostics

EXE2BIN.EXE.note: One required input and one optional output filespec

EXPAND.EXE.note: One or more explicit SZDD source files followed by a filename or directory destination; wildcards and multi-source filename destinations are rejected

FASTHELP.COM.note: DOS 6 compact-help entry point: no operand lists topics, one topic performs a case-insensitive lookup, and /? prints usage

HELP.COM.note: No operand opens the keyboard/mouse full-screen index with search and topic links; redirected output stays textual, one case-insensitive topic selects an entry, /? prints usage, and bad forms fail

LOADFIX.COM.note: One required executable plus an opaque forwarded argument tail, with child placement and status propagation

MIRROR.COM.note: Drive operands combine with snapshot modes, while deletion tracking and partition backup are exclusive forms

MSD.EXE.note: No-argument full-screen mouse/keyboard category panel plus retail /?, /B, /I, /F prompted report, /P report file, /S summary file/screen, and invalid-switch paths

MSCDEX.EXE.note: Requires one or more /D names and accepts /L, /M, /E, /K, /S, and /V; multi-subunit routing, residency, DOS file access, ISO APIs, driver forwarding, and /S shareable-drive publication are exercised

UNDELETE.COM.note: The structured textual inventory reports directory, filespec, method, file metadata, protection, and recovery result; an optional filespec selects DOS-directory, Delete Tracker, or retail-format Delete Sentry entries, with listing, automatic, and prompted recovery; /LOAD resolves and applies the executable-relative five-section INI policy, while /T, /S, /DS, /PURGE, /STATUS, and /UNLOAD expose the resident protection lifecycle

UNFORMAT.COM.note: A drive selects disk recovery and /PARTN selects partition restoration; verification and restoration have distinct confirmation behavior

IFSFUNC.EXE.note: NAMES=n accepts an allocation count from 0 through 255; overflow and repeated keywords are rejected before functional installation

INTERLNK.EXE.note: Loads with DEVICE and accepts /DRIVES:1..5, effective /NOPRINTER suppression of the BIOS and DOS printer hooks, bare, numbered, or hexadecimal-address /COM and /LPT forms, /BAUD at 9600 through 115200, /AUTO, /NOSCAN, and /V; bare port forms scan their respective port family, and command execution reports live status or /RECONNECT repeats discovery and BPB negotiation

INTERSVR.EXE.note: Up to five drive operands select exported volumes; otherwise available drives are enumerated with /X exclusions. Bare, numbered, and hexadecimal-address /COM and /LPT forms select serial or LapLink-style parallel transport, /BAUD selects a retail serial rate from 9600 through 115200, /B selects monochrome text, /V selects timer-safe polling, and /RCOPY bootstraps byte-exact executables over a MODE/CTTY serial console

LABEL.COM.marker: HEADER <GET_NEW_LABEL - PARSE NEW VOL LABEL NAME INTO PATH>
LABEL.COM.note: Optional drive and label operands plus interactive set and delete paths

MORE.COM.note: Standard-input filter with paginated console continuation rather than an operational switch grammar

NLSFUNC.EXE.note: Optional COUNTRY.SYS path, rejection forms, resident reinstallation, and path-error precedence

RECOVER.COM.note: Exactly one file-or-drive operand selecting nondestructive file or destructive volume recovery

SETUP.EXE.note: Optional directory, /Y bypass, retail /B and /F forms, excluded /E Windows form, component selection, guided installation, upgrade, generated UNINSTAL rollback, and repeat refusal are covered

SELECT.COM.note: Keyboard bootstrap stub that transfers control to SELECT.EXE and has no independent grammar

SETVER.COM.note: Optional utility path plus filename/version or /DELETE [/QUIET]; list, add, update, /DELETE, /D, quiet deletion, invalid forms, and child-visible version transitions are exercised

SYS.COM.note: One required target and one optional source operand; invalid forms are diagnosed exactly while preserving historical zero status
